traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 2, 2nd ed., 1959), family 358 Commelinaceae: perennial herbs; leaves with a closed papery sheath at the base; flowers usually regular, rarely irregular (Commelina), bisexual, in clusters in the axils or mostly in cymes or panicles at the tips, often blue or white; perianth plainly of two whorls of 3, the outer sepal-like, the inner petal-like; stamens 6 or fewer; ovary always superior, of 3 (rarely 2) cells; fruit a thin capsule, rarely fleshy.
